item.description: Wallbit oficializó su debut en Perú , junto a su cuenta global para trabajadores remotos contratados en Estados Unidos . Con ello, el país andino se suma a la lista de más d e 90 mercados donde opera la compañía , un espacio donde también México t endrá reservado un lugar para el próximo año . Directivo de l a billetera digital confirm ó a iupana su interés en coordinar alianzas con socios peruanos , como una vía para profundizar la localidad del producto.

item.title: Suspended Glencore Exec Told Radiant ‘Say Nothing on Email’
item.description: A senior Glencore Plc executive last year urged counterparts at Radiant World not to communicate by email, according to WhatsApp messages from the company’s head of iron ore seen by Bloomberg News. Hill was suspended from his duties pending the outcome of a review into Glencore’s dealings with Radiant World, Bloomberg reported on Thursday. “Say nothing on email,” Peter Hill wrote in one WhatsApp message in early April 2025.

item.title: Heat Sears Central US This Weekend as Hawaii on Flood Watch
item.description: Heat will continue to sear the Great Plains and central Mississippi Valley this weekend, as well as pushing into Texas, Oklahoma and even the eastern U.S., prompting the nation’s largest grid operator to call on customers to conserve energy. The combination of high daytime temperatures and warm nights will lead to moderate to extreme heat risk — levels 2 to 4 on a 4-step scale — across large parts of the central U.S. That includes a forecast 71F in New York’s Central Park late Friday, which would come within a degree of toppling a 1972 record for a warm night.

item.title: AIG’s Hancock to Retire as Head of General Insurance
item.description: Jon Hancock, CEO of General Insurance at American International Group (AIG), will retire at the end of the year. Hancock was named CEO of General Insurance, which includes the North America and international commercial insurance businesses and AIG’s global personal insurance book, in November 2025 once former Lloyd’s of London CEO John Neal reached a “mutual agreement” with AIG not to lead General Insurance before he was slated to start. Related: Former Lloyd’s CEO Neal Will Not Join AIG; Hancock to Be General Insurance CEO Hancock will become a senior advisor to AIG and report to Eric Anderson, president and CEO.

item.title: Driver Arrested in Bus Collision That Occurred Before Deadly LA News Copter Crash
item.description: A motorist was arrested on murder charges after authorities say she slammed her SUV into a city bus in Los Angeles, killing at least two people and injuring six others in a prelude to a second deadly tragedy: the fiery crash of a TV news helicopter that was covering the collision. Bailee Lynn Rios, 36, of Simi Valley, was arrested Tuesday night and was being held at a Los Angeles jail with bail set at $4 million, police said Wednesday. The helicopter, which was used by NBC and Telemundo, crashed about two hours after police say Rios drove her 2004 Ford Expedition the wrong way down a busy avenue, ran a red light and struck a vehicle before hitting the bus.

item.title: Starbucks Settles Florida Lawsuit Claiming Diversity Policies Were Illegal
item.description: A federal judge dismissed a similar lawsuit in February by the Missouri Attorney General’s office targeting Starbucks’ alleged diversity policies. Starbucks agreed on Thursday to settle a discrimination lawsuit by the state of Florida, pledging not to adopt race- or sex-based quotas or preferences in hiring, promotion and pay decisions. Starbucks and Florida’s Republican Attorney General James Uthmeier jointly announced the settlement of a lawsuit filed by the state last December.

item.title: What 25,000 Startup Applications Reveal About The New Rules Of Seed-Stage Startups
item.description: Ten years ago, a seed-stage startup needed a product, a team and a pitch deck to raise capital. Here are the key shifts we’re seeing in the startup ecosystem at the seed stage. The breakout companies are investing in building stronger distribution systems — aka what founders refer to as “traction.” Distribution is a critical moat for early-stage startups.

item.title: Swiss Re supporting clients by creating risk awareness, prevention and transfer: Urs Baertschi
item.description: Urs Baertschi, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Property & Casualty (P&C) Reinsurance at Swiss Re emphasised that within today’s increasingly interconnected world, the reinsurer is supporting clients by creating risk awareness, risk prevention, and risk transfer. And those three steps-the risk awareness, the risk prevention, and the risk transfer-of is how we show up to our end clients.” Baertschi then discussed the lines of business that Swiss Re sees the greatest opportunities and challenges for over the next 12 months. “This comes down to what we do in our industry in terms of creating risk awareness, risk prevention, and risk transfer, all three of those are absolutely critical in our industry and how we bring value to society,” he explained.

item.title: Moody’s launches Risk InvestorIQ to support ILS transaction and portfolio evaluation
item.description: “And as activity grows, investors need analytical capabilities that can evaluate transactions in the context of an entire portfolio while keeping pace with increasing transaction volumes.” He continued: “To help, Moody’s has extended the catastrophe risk analytics ecosystem already used by insurers, reinsurers, and other industry participants; the launch of Risk InvestorIQ now brings ILS workflows to Moody’s Intelligent Risk Platform™, delivering a dedicated environment for ILS investors and risk professionals to evaluate transactions and gauge their portfolio impact.” The Associate Director also observed that many firms still choose to use and rely on legacy workflows that span multiple systems, and take up valuable time as users transfer data, reconcile outputs, and move between applications before they can compare transactions or determine their potential effect on a portfolio. To combat this friction, Moody’s states that Risk InvestorIQ places deal evaluation, portfolio analytics, and portfolio management together within one dedicated ILS environment. Moody’s has launched Risk InvestorIQ, a dedicated catastrophe risk analytics and portfolio management application to provide ILS investors and risk professionals with an environment to evaluate transactions and gauge their portfolio impact.

item.title: Casualty sidecars require discipline on both sides as asset risk grows: Ledger
item.description: As asset-driven sidecars expand in the casualty market, focus is shifting from capital efficiency to risk management. Given this, Ledger Investing indicates that turning collateral into a second source of return requires market participants to underwrite the supporting asset portfolio with the same discipline as the liabilities. The insurtech and casualty ILS specialist shared these details in a recently published report, which examined the rise of asset-driven sidecars, how the economics surrounding them works, and what their growth could mean for the expanding casualty ILS market.

item.title: Buffett Steps Down as Berkshire Chair, Ending Six-Decade Run
item.description: founder Warren Buffett is stepping down as the company’s chairman to be replaced by his son Howard, effectively ending roughly six decades at the helm of the conglomerate. The elder Buffett will remain a member of the board, while his son, a director of the company since 1993, steps into the top role. “The culture Warren built and the values he championed will remain at the heart of Berkshire, and Howard will be their guardian.” Buffett, 96, transformed the Omaha, Nebraska-based company, once an aging textile mill, into a more than $1 trillion conglomerate.

item.title: New York Developers Look North of Miami for Florida’s Next Boom
item.description: After years of trying to convince developers and investors that it’s a viable alternative to Miami and Palm Beach, Fort Lauderdale’s pitch is starting to resonate. Much of the work is planned and financed by deep-pocketed New York developers betting that Fort Lauderdale’s time has finally come. Some of the new residents may be drawn by Florida’s lower overall taxes, but soaring costs in Miami may make its northern neighbor more attractive.

item.title: Florida Home Sellers Cutting Prices Adds to Pressure on Lennar
item.description: It’s especially notable in Florida and Texas, two of Lennar’s largest markets, Chief Executive Officer Stuart Miller said on a call with analysts Thursday. That gave homebuilders including Lennar an advantage. Lennar focuses on building affordable homes, pitched at buyers who are sensitive to mortgage rates, which now stand at their highest levels in more than a year.

item.title: AXA Hong Kong and Macau partners with BytePlus on AI
item.description: AXA Hong Kong and Macau has signed an agreement with enterprise technology provider BytePlus to develop and deploy AI solutions across the insurance value chain. David Ng, deputy chief executive officer of AXA Hong Kong and Macau, said the partnership marked a significant step for the insurer’s AI ambitions. AXA will also use BytePlus’s predictive analytics and consumer persona modelling to improve customer insights and personalise interactions.

item.title: Mosaic launches HALO digital underwriting system
item.description: Mosaic Insurance has launched HALO, a digital underwriting system designed to quickly bring complex specialty products to the small and midsize enterprise (SME) market. It will also be increasingly relevant as we expand HALO into our other specialty products with their own aggregation and concentration risks.” The new Cyber Tech E&O offering combines HALO’s digital underwriting capabilities with Mosaic’s cyber expertise, in-house claims authority, 24-hour incident response, and Lloyd’s-backed financial strength. “HALO reflects our broader AI strategy: using technology to augment underwriting, leverage data, and enable our teams to deploy their expertise more efficiently and at greater scale.” Liam Jones, chief executive officer of Mosaic’s agency business, said the platform provided infrastructure not commonly available today.

item.title: Equal Parts acquires ProSource Insurance Agency
item.description: Equal Parts has acquired ProSource Insurance Agency, a Plano, Texas-based brokerage specializing in transportation insurance. Among Equal Parts’ previous acquisitions are Blue Star Insurance Agency and Strategic Insurance, both based in New Mexico. ProSource will continue operating under Nhem’s leadership while gaining access to Equal Parts’ technology, centralized operations, carrier relationships, shared services and acquisition resources.

item.title: TruePoint Systems partners With SeedPod Cyber
item.description: Texas technology and cybersecurity provider TruePoint Systems has partnered with cyber insurance MGA SeedPod Cyber to connect security assessments and remediation with the insurance-placement process. SeedPod’s licensed insurance professionals will handle quoting and place coverage through its carrier partners. SeedPod specializes in cyber insurance and risk management.

item.title: Ayble Health raises $16 million
item.description: The company says it is in-network with most commercial health plans and reaches more than 80 million people through partnerships. Founded by inflammatory bowel disease patient Sam Jactel, Ayble has raised more than $27 million to date. Ayble combines clinical care and technology to support patients with gastrointestinal conditions.

item.title: Credit Acceptance Reaches $710M Predatory Auto Lending Settlement With Most States
item.description: The settlement announced on Thursday also resolves claims that Credit Acceptance, one of the nation’s largest subprime auto lenders, helped car dealers push consumers to buy unnecessary add-on products, such as vehicle service contracts, and insurance that they did not need or were never told about. to resolve charges it drove thousands of borrowers with low incomes and low credit scores into predatory auto loans it knew they could not afford. Credit Acceptance will forgive $634 million of debt owed by more than 55,000 borrowers who took out loans between November 2015 and November 2025, pay $60 million in restitution to thousands of other borrowers, and pay a $15.5 million penalty, New York Attorney General Letitia James said.

item.title: Swiss Re: 100 Years After Miami Hurricane, Similar Storm Would Top $200B in Losses
item.description: “That lesson extends well beyond Florida: As populations and asset values increase in areas exposed to natural catastrophes, so does the potential for large insured losses.” And 34 years after Hurricane Andrew made landfall near Miami and changed building codes and construction practices in the state, a similar storm would produce almost $100 billion in insured losses, Swiss Re estimated. If the storm were to develop into a Category 5 hurricane that strikes heavily populated cities like Miami or Tampa Bay, the insured losses could top $300 billion—more than any previous insured-loss event, Swiss Re said in a report released this week. “One hundred years after the Great Miami Hurricane, the question is not simply how powerful the next major hurricane will be, but what it will encounter when it reaches shore,” Balz Grollimund, head of catastrophe perils at Swiss Re said in the report this week.

item.title: Lucid, Bolt Team up to Deploy 25,000 Robotaxis Across Europe
item.description: EV maker Lucid Group and European shared mobility platform Bolt said on Thursday they are teaming up to roll out self-driving ride services across Europe, as they seek to tap into the region’s emerging robotaxi market. Bolt plans to deploy 25,000 fully autonomous Lucid vehicles in major European cities as part of a broader push to grow its autonomous fleet to 100,000 vehicles by 2035. Lucid and Bolt will co-develop an autonomous-driving-system-ready vehicle platform designed for SAE Level 4 automation, meaning the vehicles can operate with no intervention within defined operating conditions and areas.

item.title: Building a stronger UK investment culture
item.description: A stronger investment culture will not be built by any one organisation alone. When we talk about building a healthier investment culture in the UK, we mean helping people get the support, clear information and suitable choices they need to make confident decisions. Above all, we mean building trust, so people can plan for their financial future with greater confidence.

item.title: Discipline determines the credit outcome of soft reinsurance market pricing: KBRA
item.description: The benefits of a soft reinsurance market environment are not automatic for protection buyers, KBRA cautions, and it is management transmission that matters. Lower priced catastrophe reinsurance cover should not be viewed as a signal that risk has declined and while the market is awash with both traditional and alternative reinsurance capital it’s important P&C insurers maintain their discipline “Savings used to strengthen protection or retained capital are more credit supportive than savings used to fund aggressive catastrophe-exposed growth, materially higher net retentions, or shareholder distributions,” the rating agency explained. “Conversely, much of the benefit can be lost if favorable reinsurance economics encourage aggressive exposure growth, higher retained risk, weaker primary pricing discipline, or increased capital distributions,” KBRA said.

item.title: Flexibility will be rewarded as capacity floods market: Kumar, Marsh Securities CEO
item.description: Insurance-linked securities investors must broaden their mandates or risk losing relevance with cedents in a softening reinsurance market flush with capacity, according to Shiv Kumar, CEO of Marsh Securities, speaking in an interview at the 2026 Rendez-Vous de Septembre. Speaking with Artemis at the 68th edition of the event in Monaco, Kumar observed that the catastrophe bond market has performed well for investors in recent years. “That increased optionality, a broader capacity base, and greater diversity across their programs are all clear benefits for clients,” Kumar said.

item.title: Gorman Named PIA National President
item.description: The National Association of Professional Insurance Agents has made David Gorman its president, succeeding Mark Suhr. Joining Gorman as national officers are Vonda Copeland of Manhattan, Kansas, as president-elect; Albert S. Gorman, of Dallas, founded Red Gorman Insurance Services in 2018 and has a long history of service to the independent insurance agent community holding various leadership roles in the PIA of Texas and PIA National.

item.title: White House Weighs Incubator for Cyber Research, Startups
item.description: The White House’s Office of the National Cyber Director has been drafting an executive order that would establish a program to research and develop cyber technologies that are aligned with the priorities of the US government, the people said, asking not to be identified because the plans aren’t yet public. The Trump administration is weighing a plan to establish a government-led incubator aimed at investing in cybersecurity research and spinning out startups focused on developing tools for the government to use, according to people familiar with the situation. Inside the US government, the effort has been compared with the way Israel closely aligns its military priorities with the focus of cybersecurity startups, venture capital investments and academic research in the country, according to the people familiar with the plans.

AXA will also use BytePlus’s predictive analytics and consumer persona modeling to improve customer insights and personalize interactions. “We aim to co-innovate specialised, insurance-specific AI models that drive industry-wide transformation.” BytePlus is the enterprise technology unit of TikTok parent ByteDance.

item.title: ProLiant expands Employee Navigator partnership
item.description: Payroll and human capital management provider ProLiant has become an Employee Navigator licensee, allowing employers to access the benefits administration platform directly through ProLiant. ProLiant has integrated with Employee Navigator for nearly a decade and currently supports two-way API connectivity and single sign-on. The option is intended for employers that do not already receive Employee Navigator through a benefits broker.

item.title: The Technology Taking Parametric Insurance Mainstream
item.description: Parametric insurance is entering the mainstream. Research & Markets’ Parametric Insurance Market Report 2026 , for example, estimated the global parametric insurance market was worth $21.09bn in 2025 and forecast it to reach $23.85bn in 2026. This year, a series of market reports and industry developments call out a clear trend.

item.title: OneShield Pre-Integrates Input 1 Payments
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) Input 1 (Westlake Village, Calif.) and OneShield (Marlborough, Mass.) have entered an agreement making Input 1’s digital payments and premium finance capabilities pre-integrated with the OneShield platform. The integration enables carriers, MGAs and program administrators running OneShield to adopt Input 1 digital payments and premium finance without sourcing and connecting the capabilities separately, according to a joint statement. Jones runs Input 1 digital payments within OneShield.

item.title: Georgia Farm Bureau Selects ZestyAI
item.description: Georgia Farm Bureau Selects Akur8’s Core Platform ZestyAI Supports Three California Homeowners Programs (Image source: Georgia Farm Bureau Mutual Insurance Company website.) Georgia Farm Bureau Mutual Insurance Company (Macon, Ga.) has selected ZestyAI’s (San Francisco) ZORRO Discover platform to support actuarial, regulatory, competitive intelligence and product development workflows. “Georgia Farm Bureau Mutual Insurance Company has spent more than 65 years learning its farm families better than anyone,” comments Attila Toth, Founder and CEO, ZestyAI.

item.title: Torrential Rain Brings Deadly Floods Back to East Coast of Spain
item.description: Torrential rain lashed the east coast of Spain, flooding roads and leaving at least one person dead. The heavy rainfall started Wednesday in Valencia and Catalonia, reviving fears of a repeat of the devastating floods that killed more than 200 people in 2024. At the end of October 2024, an intense “dana” storm — a common phenomenon in Spain at the time of year — devastated the Valencia region.

item.title: Emerging Risks to Watch: Quantum Computing, Data Center Buildout, and Peptides
item.description: These may range from commercial inland marine risks associated with the transportation of high-value quantum computing equipment to potential litigation risks related to the statements and disclosures made by directors and officers in the quantum computing supply chain. Present-day quantum computing services increasingly rely on the physical and computational infrastructure of modern data centers. Emerging risks rarely arrive fully formed.

item.title: China Construction Bank manager pleads guilty to accepting bribes from Vesttoo employee
item.description: In a turn of events, the first criminal charges related to the reinsurance letters of credit fraud have finally been confirmed, as a former China Construction Bank employee has pleaded guilty to accepting bribes to authenticate false collateral documentation. Back in June 2025 a Hong Kong bribery case took aim at the former China Construction Bank relationship manager , when the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region charged him with “allegedly conspiring with an employee of a fintech company to use various false standby letters of credit (L/Cs) and collateral letters,” that fintech being Vesttoo. The ICAC stated, “Lam Chun-yin, 32, former relationship manager of China Construction Bank (Asia) Corporation Limited (CCB (Asia)), pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy for an agent to accept advantages, contrary to section 9(1)(a) of the Prevention of Bribery Ordinance and section 159A of the Crimes Ordinance.

item.title: ExxonMobil Wins Approval for Texas Carbon Capture in 2-to-1 Vote
item.description: won approval for its Rose carbon-capture project in Texas, allowing the company to move ahead with the emission-reducing development that could be among the biggest of its kind. The Railroad Commission of Texas, the state’s primary oil and natural gas regulator, approved a permit to inject carbon dioxide underground with two commissioners voting in support and one against, according to a statement release by dissenting member Wayne Christian. The permit allows ExxonMobil to inject as much as 53 million tons of carbon dioxide over a 13-year period from industrial emitters along the Gulf Coast into rock strata about one mile (1.6 kilometers) underground for permanent storage.

item.title: Senate Committee Sends TRIA Reauthorization to the Floor
item.description: At the end of July, a large group of organizations including NAMIC, the American Property Casualty Insurance Association, the Independent Insurance Agents & Brokers of America, the Reinsurance Association of America, the Wholesale & Specialty Insurance Association, the Council of Insurance Agents & Brokers, and the Vermont Captive Insurance Association sent a letter to Senate leaders urging them “to avoid market disruptions and continue the economic certainty provided by the program.” “Completion of congressional action on a long-term reauthorization of TRIA comes at a time when organizations are taking a fresh look at geopolitical risk. Federal legislation to extend the Terrorism Risk Insurance Act will head to the full Senate after unanimously getting a nod from the Senate Banking Committee. 4395, the Terrorism Risk Insurance Program Reauthorization Act of 2026.

item.title: Chubb names new digital business leaders
item.description: Chubb has appointed Johan Oosthuizen global head of digital business, giving him responsibility for the insurer’s digital operations, including partnership acquisition and performance and product deployment. Lazaro joined Chubb in 2016 as head of digital for Latin America and most recently served as head of digital business for Overseas General Insurance. Oosthuizen previously served as Chubb’s global digital chief technology officer, where he helped build the company’s embedded insurance and digital partnership capabilities.

item.title: Hershey Defeats Reese’s Lawsuit Over Halloween Pumpkins That Lacked ‘Cool’ Carvings
item.description: Hershey won the dismissal of a lawsuit claiming it let down consumers because its Halloween-themed Reese’s pumpkins lacked the decorative carved designs shown on the packaging. “Plaintiffs do not allege that the Hershey’s Reese’s Peanut Butter Pumpkins that they purchased were defective or worthless or that they lost all economic value because of the absence of the decorative carvings.” The judge also said Vidal and Granados could not show they paid up to 25% too much by citing Reese’s prices at Target, at Walmart and in Hershey’s online store, because they bought their candy at a Publix supermarket. In a court filing seeking the lawsuit’s dismissal, Hershey said its packaging included a disclaimer that the depicted carvings were a “decorating suggestion.”

item.title: Satellites Show Earth Lost More Than 12T Tons of Ice in 47 Years
item.description: About 12.5 trillion tons (11.3 trillion metric tons) of ice from glaciers in Greenland and Antarctica have melted since 1979, which is enough frozen water to stack ice 5 feet (1.5 meters) deep across the continental United States, according to a major scientific report. A warming Earth is accelerating the melting of the planet’s two major ice sheets, with five-sixths of the melt not coming from hotter air, but from warmer waters eating away at the ice sheets from below and the sides, with glaciers flowing into the oceans, according to a study in Wednesday’s journal Scientific Data. But by incorporating NASA satellites, the scientists were able to chart ice sheet volumes in Antarctica back to 1979 and in Greenland back to 1972.

item.title: UK Insurers Urge Bank of England to Rethink ‘Dynamic’ Stress Test
item.description: Britain’s insurance industry is urging the Bank of England’s regulatory arm to rethink its live crisis simulation, citing heavy reporting demands and unrealistic scenarios in a stress test that pushed firms “to their absolute limit.” The Prudential Regulation Authority’s first “dynamic” stress test, which ran over three weeks in May, subjected insurers to successive crises including a U.S. Unlike previous stress tests that assessed how insurers would handle predefined shocks, this one – known as DyGIST – tested insurers’ ability to respond in real time to adverse conditions as they unfold, with scenario details revealed only during the live exercise. “The accumulation of scenarios in such a short time frame was very unlikely,” said Nafisah Hussain, director of public policy at the International Underwriting Association, a trade body for insurers and reinsurers in the London market that has fed its views back to the PRA.

item.title: FDA Declares Cyclospora Outbreak Over
item.description: The Cyclospora outbreak that impacted people in more than 21 states has been declared over by the U.S. Though the outbreak is over, the FDA continues the outbreak investigation of Cyclospora infections linked to iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico and recalled by Taylor Farms de Mexico. Since the last update on August 27, 2026, state and local health officials have continued to interview additional sick people with Cyclosporiasis and the CDC has added them to this multi-state outbreak.

item.title: Financial crime: protecting the hive
item.description: Speaker: Steve Smart, executive director of enforcement and market oversight Event: Law Society Economic Crime Conference 2026 Delivered: 17 September 2026 Note: This is a drafted speech and may differ from the delivered version Reading time: 7 minutes A few weeks ago, I visited the Bank of England Museum to see a new exhibition on financial crime. That same instinct and partnership are what we need to fight financial crime. The criminals we’re up against don’t present themselves for checking, and the system we’re protecting is much larger than a hive.
